1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 a6 4.Ba4 Nf6 5.O.name: Ruy Lopez: Morphy Defence, Steinitz Deferred
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 a6 4.Ba4 Nf6 5.O.background: Mikhail Chigorin played it in the 1890s, and Akiba Rubinstein and Alekhine adopted it later; its last significant use was by some Russian masters in the 1950s.

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Bb5 a6 4.Ba4 Nf6 5.O.strategy: Takes the knight with check while Black's d-pawn has already moved, so the natural recapture is with the b-pawn, which breaks up the queenside. White then opens lines in the centre quickly, aiming to profit from Black's undeveloped pieces.

The natural recapture, since the d-pawn is already on d6: the c-pawns double and the queenside is damaged, but Black gets the bishop pair and the half-open b-file. Black has to play actively, as White's quick central play punishes any lag in development.
